label: Video production
project: Spring product launch brand film (60s + 3 cutdowns)
summary: A 60-second hero film plus 15s and 30s social cutdowns for a skincare product launch.
billing: 50% deposit to book crew and dates, 50% on final delivery (Net 30); larger commercial jobs split 40% booking / 30% after first cut / 30% on final. 2-3 revision rounds included, extra rounds billed. Sources: liveupmedia T&Cs, filmlifestyle contract guide.
ms: Pre-production: script, treatment and shot list
Done means the client has signed off the script, treatment, shot list, location and talent, and the shoot date is locked.
Done means all scheduled scenes are captured, footage is backed up twice and the client rep has seen playback on set.
Client on-set approval of key shots
Footage offloaded and double backed up
Post-production: rough cut and fine cut
Done means the client has given consolidated notes on the rough cut and approved the fine cut (picture lock).
Rough cut v1 delivered for review
Done means color, sound mix, music license and graphics are final and all masters and cutdowns are delivered in the agreed formats.
Master files and license docs delivered
waiting: Consolidated feedback on the rough cut (one set of timestamped notes from all stakeholders).
ask: Which music track should we license for the hero film?
Both licenses cover web and paid social for 1 year; Track C costs $350 more.
answered: The client's flagship studio in Pasadena, not a rented stage.
checkin: - Done: shoot wrapped, all 22 setups captured and backed up
- Next: rough cut v1 on Friday for review
- Needs from you: final product claims copy for the end card, and pick a music track
talk: Rough cut v1 is up in the review link. Please leave timestamped notes and send one combined list from your team by Wednesday.
Looks great. Marketing wants the logo earlier and legal flagged the 'clinically proven' line.
Got it. We'll move the logo to 0:04 and swap the line for the approved claim. Fine cut Monday.
anxieties: When will I see a first cut?
How many changes can we still make, and what costs extra?
Do we own the footage and can we use it in paid ads / for how long (music license)?
notes: Highly variable scope (1-day shoot to multi-week campaign). Portal must handle timestamped review on video versions (v1, v2, lock), counted revision rounds, a picture-lock approval, music/usage license documents, and large-file delivery with multiple aspect ratios. Raw footage ownership is a common separate line item.

label: Commercial / brand photography
project: Fall catalog and e-commerce product shoot (40 SKUs)
summary: Studio product shots on white plus 8 lifestyle images for a home goods brand's fall launch.
billing: Estimate separates creative fee, usage license, and expenses (assistants, styling, props, retouching); typical 50% advance to book, balance on delivery. Usage is priced by media, territory, duration and exclusivity. Sources: ASMP sample estimate, Fstoppers license-fee guide, Digital Photography School.
ms: Estimate, usage and shot list approved
Done means the client signed the estimate with the usage license defined and approved the shot list and creative direction.
Shot list of 40 SKUs plus 8 lifestyle
Done means every shot on the list is captured and the art director approved key frames on tether.
Lighting setup approved on first SKU
Done means the client has picked their selects from the online proof gallery.
Done means retouched finals are delivered in the agreed sizes and the license document is issued.
waiting: Selects marked in the proof gallery (and the physical products shipped to the studio before the shoot).
ask: How long should the usage license run?
Paid ads and print are priced separately.
answered: Pure white for marketplace listings, plus a warm grey set for the website.
checkin: - Done: shoot complete, 312 proofs in your gallery
- Next: retouching starts as soon as selects are in
- Needs from you: heart your selects by Thursday, max 60 images
talk: Proofs are live. Please heart the frames you want retouched; 60 are included.
We loved more than 60. Can we add some?
Yes, extra retouched images are $25 each. Mark them and I'll add them to the final invoice.
anxieties: When do we get finals?
Where we can use the images (ads, print, Amazon) and for how long
How many images and retouches are included
notes: Usage rights are a first-class object: the portal should show licensed media, territory and expiry next to the files. Proof gallery with selects and comments, included-image counts with paid overages, and product check-in/return for shipped items.

label: Wedding photography and videography
project: Priya and Jordan wedding, full-day photo + highlight film
summary: 10 hours of coverage with two photographers and a videographer, engagement session and a 5-minute highlight film.
billing: Non-refundable retainer of 25-50% to hold the date, balance due 2-4 weeks before the wedding (some take payment plans). Gallery in 4-8 weeks, sneak peek within days. Sources: Albany Capture (Pixieset blog), Bonsai wedding contract, Susan Stripling, Imagen AI.
ms: Done means the contract is signed and the retainer is paid, so the date is reserved.
Done means the engagement shoot is delivered and the wedding-day questionnaire and timeline are final.
Done means the balance was paid before the wedding and full-day coverage is complete.
Getting ready to grand exit covered
Done means the full edited gallery and the highlight film are delivered and download links work.
waiting: The wedding-day questionnaire with the family formals list and the final day-of timeline.
ask: Do you want to add a second videographer for the ceremony?
Gives a second angle on vows and the processional.
checkin: - Done: engagement gallery delivered
- Next: final timeline call 3 weeks before the wedding
- Needs from you: questionnaire and family formals list, balance due April 15
talk: Hi Priya! Can you send the family formals list and your planner's timeline by next Friday?
Will do. When will we get our photos after the wedding?
Sneak peek within 3 days, full gallery within 6 weeks, and the highlight film within 10 weeks.
anxieties: When will we get our photos / film?
Is the balance due date and amount right?
Do you have our timeline, shot list and vendor contacts?
notes: Long gaps: 6-18 months from booking to event, then 1-3 months to delivery, which is where 'where are my photos?' messages spike. Portal must show payment plan, questionnaire forms, a delivery ETA after the event, gallery links, album proof approvals. Usage is personal; photographer keeps copyright. Last milestone often has no new payment because the balance is due pre-event.

label: Wedding planning
summary: Full-service planning for a 150-guest vineyard wedding in Sonoma next September.
billing: Non-refundable retainer at booking, then installments tied to planning stages, final balance about 30 days before the wedding; fees are flat ($4k-12k full service) or 10-20% of event spend. Vendor money tracked separately. Sources: SchedulingKit wedding planners, eventplanning.com price list template.
ms: Done means the contract and retainer are in, budget is set and the vision deck is approved.
Done means venue, caterer, photographer, florist and music are contracted.
Done means invitations are out, menu tasting is done and the floor plan and decor are final.
Done means the final balance is paid, all vendors have the run-of-show, and the day is executed.
Final guest count and seating chart
waiting: RSVP-based final guest count and the seating chart.
ask: Which florist do you want to book?
Proposals are in the design board.
answered: On the vineyard lawn, with the barn as rain backup.
checkin: - Done: caterer and band booked, tasting scheduled for May 3
- Next: invitation proofs from the stationer
- Needs from you: sign the florist proposal and send your guest address list
talk: We have three florist proposals in your design board. Bloom Theory has the date open only until Friday.
We love Bloom Theory but it's over budget. Can they trim it?
I asked them to swap peonies for garden roses; that brings it to $8,400. Sending the revised proposal now.
anxieties: Are we on budget?
What decisions are due next and by when?
Which vendors are booked and paid?
notes: Many parallel tracks and many decisions; the portal is more a decision-and-checklist tracker than a deliverables tracker. Must show budget vs actual, vendor list with contracts and due payments (vendor money separate from planner fee), guest list/RSVP, and a countdown timeline.

label: Event planning (corporate)
summary: Two-day sales kickoff with a general session, breakouts, an awards dinner and room block.
billing: Flat management fee or 10-20% of event budget (hourly $50-150 for small jobs); commonly 50% at booking, 25% at 30 days out, 25% on or within 7 days after the event. Vendor costs passed through or contracted directly. Sources: Event Smart, Chron, invoicequickly template.
ms: Done means the venue and hotel block are contracted and the budget and agenda framework are approved.
Done means AV, catering, transport and the registration site are booked and live.
Done means the run-of-show, signage, speaker slides and rooming list are final.
Signage and badges sent to print
Done means the event ran, final vendor invoices are reconciled and the wrap report is delivered.
waiting: Final attendee list and speaker slides by the deadline.
ask: Which awards dinner format should we book?
checkin: - Done: registration live, 212 of 300 registered
- Next: AV walkthrough and run-of-show v2
- Needs from you: speaker list with session titles, F&B guarantee by Jan 20
talk: Run-of-show v2 is in the portal. We still need slide decks from 4 speakers by Jan 26.
I'll chase them. Can we add a 15-minute CEO Q&A after the keynote?
Yes. I've added it at 9:45 and shifted breakouts by 15 minutes; AV confirmed a second handheld mic.
anxieties: Budget vs actual (overages, F&B minimums, attrition)
Registration numbers and room block pickup
Is everything on schedule for the deadlines?
notes: Heavy deadline management (attrition dates, F&B guarantees). Portal should show budget, registration count, decisions and the run-of-show; files are contracts and run-of-show versions. Many stakeholders on the client side.

label: Graphic design and branding
summary: New logo, color, type, packaging labels and a brand guide for a coffee roaster's rebrand.
billing: 50% non-refundable deposit to start, balance on final approval (some 60/40 or thirds by phase); 2-3 logo concepts and 2 revision rounds typical, extra rounds hourly. Sources: Bonsai branding contract, Contra/Dribbble service listings.
ms: Done means the client approved the brand strategy summary (audience, positioning, attributes).
Done means the client picked one logo direction out of three concepts.
Done means the final logo, palette, type and pattern are approved after two rounds of revisions.
Done means the brand guide and all logo files are delivered and ownership transferred on final payment.
Logo files AI, EPS, SVG, PNG, PDF
waiting: Consolidated feedback on the logo concepts (one decision, not separate notes from each partner).
ask: Which logo direction should we refine?
Two refinement rounds are included on the one you pick.
answered: Warm terracotta with cream, not the old navy.
checkin: - Done: 3 concepts presented on Tuesday
- Next: refinement round 1 on the chosen direction
- Needs from you: pick a direction and send combined feedback
talk: All three concepts are in the review board. Please pick one direction to move forward.
We like A but want the badge shape from C. Can you combine them?
Yes, we can merge them in round 1. That uses the first of your two included revision rounds.
anxieties: How many revisions do we get?
When will we have final files to give the printer?
Do we own the logo / do we get the source files?
notes: Revision-round counter is essential and a top dispute source. Proof/review with markup on images and PDFs, concept voting, a final approval event, and file delivery that unlocks on final payment (IP transfer).

label: Web design and development
summary: 10-page WordPress site with online booking, new photography and SEO basics.
billing: 25-50% deposit at kickoff, then milestones at design approval, development complete and launch (e.g. 40/30/30). Legal guides warn against bare 50/50. Late fee about 1.5% per month. Sources: SchedulingKit web designers, Sprintlaw AU and UK.
ms: Done means the sitemap, page list and content plan are approved.
Content plan and who writes what
Done means the home page and inner page designs are approved after revisions.
Done means all pages are built on staging with real content and booking working.
Done means the site is live on the domain, forms tested, and training and handover done.
waiting: Website content: page copy, team bios and photos (content is the number-one launch delay).
ask: Which booking system should the site connect to?
answered: WordPress, so the front desk can edit pages.
checkin: - Done: design approved, staging site built
- Next: load content and test booking
- Needs from you: bios and headshots for 4 dentists, and domain registrar login
talk: Staging is ready, but 4 pages are waiting on your copy. Can you send it by Friday to keep the launch date?
The team bios are late. Can you write placeholder bios?
We can draft them from their LinkedIn profiles for you to approve; that's a 2-hour add-on.
anxieties: When does the site go live?
What are you waiting on from us?
Can we make changes after launch, and what will that cost?
notes: Client-blocking content and logins are the main delays; the portal should make 'waiting on you' items explicit with due dates. Staging link reviews with comments, revision rounds on design, credentials collection (securely), and post-launch maintenance retainer upsell.

label: App development
summary: A booking and workout-tracking MVP for a chain of fitness studios, built in React Native.
billing: Payment on signature covering discovery and first sprint, then per two-week sprint, final payment on App Store approval and launch; client owns code after final payment. Sources: Bonsai app development contract, Dribbble service listings.
ms: Done means user flows, wireframes and the feature backlog for the MVP are approved.
Done means high-fidelity screens and the design system are approved.
Done means all MVP features are built and a beta is on TestFlight and Google internal testing.
Done means the client accepted the beta, the apps passed store review and are live.
waiting: Beta feedback and acceptance sign-off (plus App Store developer account access).
ask: Should Apple Pay be in the MVP or phase 2?
Card payments via Stripe already ship in the MVP.
answered: React Native for both iOS and Android from one codebase.
checkin: - Done: sprint 2 demo, booking works end to end
- Next: sprint 3 workout tracking
- Needs from you: add us to your Apple Developer account and approve the class schedule API access
talk: Sprint 2 demo video and a TestFlight build are up. Please log bugs in the feedback form.
The booking flow works. Can we add a waitlist?
A waitlist is new scope. I'll estimate it as a change request so you can decide on MVP or phase 2.
anxieties: Are we on track for the launch date?
Is this new request in scope or extra?
Who owns the code and accounts?
notes: Sprint-based; progress is best shown as sprint demos and a burn-down of scope. Change requests need their own approve/decline flow with price. Portal must handle build links (TestFlight), bug reports, account access handover and IP transfer on final payment. Projects vary hugely ($20k-500k+).

label: Marketing and social media agency
summary: Monthly social for a boutique hotel: 16 posts, 8 reels, community management and reporting on Instagram and TikTok.
billing: Monthly retainer billed in advance ($1k-5k for small businesses), often 3-month minimum; ad spend, stock and production billed separately. Approval rounds drive cost. Sources: Cloud Campaign, Kontentino, Taskade SOW.
ms: Done means the client approved the October content calendar and campaign themes.
Done means all posts and reels for the month are created and approved by the client.
Done means everything is scheduled and published and comments and DMs are handled daily.
Done means the performance report is delivered and reviewed on the monthly call.
waiting: Approval of the scheduled posts in the content calendar (plus raw photos or event info for the month).
ask: We'll build the November calendar around your pick.
answered: Instagram and TikTok only; Facebook is mirrored from Instagram.
checkin: - Done: 12 of 16 posts approved and scheduled
- Next: reels from the spa shoot
- Needs from you: approve the 4 remaining posts and confirm Halloween event details
talk: 4 posts are waiting for your approval in the calendar. They go live starting Monday.
Approved 3. For the bar post, can we use the new cocktail menu photo?
Swapped. It's scheduled for Tuesday at 6pm.
anxieties: What's going out this week, and has it been approved?
Is it working (followers, reach, bookings)?
What am I paying for this month / ad spend
notes: Recurring; progress resets monthly, so the portal should show 'this month' with a calendar and per-post approval status, a report at month end, and history of past months. Approvals per post with comments, ad spend tracked separately from fee. Amount only on the month-end invoice line because the retainer is billed once per month.

label: SEO agency
project: Q1 SEO program for Patel Plumbing
summary: Local SEO retainer: audit fixes, 4 service-area pages a month, Google Business Profile and monthly reporting.
billing: Monthly retainer billed in advance ($500-7,500 for small and mid businesses), often with a one-time onboarding audit fee; 3-12 month minimums common; about 78% of providers bill by retainer (Ahrefs survey, cited). Sources: The Admin Bar, DesignRush, Bonsai SEO contract.
ms: Done means the technical audit and keyword research are delivered and the 90-day roadmap is approved.
Done means the priority audit fixes are live and on-page optimizations are published.
Done means this month's service-area pages are published and citations and links are built.
Done means the rankings and traffic report is delivered and reviewed on the call.
waiting: CMS and Google Search Console / Analytics access, then approval of drafted page content.
ask: Which service area pages should we write first?
Based on search volume, emergency plumbing is highest.
checkin: - Done: audit fixes live, site speed up from 48 to 81
- Next: 4 location pages this month
- Needs from you: approve the drain cleaning draft, add us as a GBP manager
talk: Rankings for 'plumber Fremont' moved from 14 to 8. Your next 2 pages are in review.
Why aren't we in the map pack yet?
Map pack depends heavily on reviews; you have 31 vs competitors' 120. We're launching a review request text this week.
anxieties: When will we see results / are rankings moving?
What did you actually do this month?
Are leads and calls going up?
notes: Results lag effort by months, so the portal's value is showing work done plus trend lines. Monthly cycle like the social agency; first month includes onboarding audit. Access/credentials collection and content approvals are the client's main tasks.

label: Music production and recording studio
summary: Recording, production, mixing and mastering for a 5-song indie pop EP.
billing: 50% non-refundable deposit to book sessions, balance before final WAV release; mixing often per song with 2 revision rounds, extra revisions or analog recalls about $75 per song. Sources: Depot Sound mixing agreement, Classick Studios rates, Necromorbus Studio.
ms: Done means the songs, arrangements, tempos and session schedule are locked.
Done means drums, bass, guitars, keys and vocals are recorded for all 5 songs.
Done means the artist approved the mix of each song after up to 2 revision rounds.
Done means masters, instrumentals and stems are delivered after the final balance.
waiting: Mix notes on each song (with timestamps), then approval to send to mastering.
ask: Which vocal take should we use on the bridge of Song 3?
Both are in the session folder for comparison.
checkin: - Done: all tracking finished, mixes v1 for 5 songs uploaded
- Next: mix revisions once notes are in
- Needs from you: timestamped notes per song by Sunday
talk: Mix v1 for all 5 songs is up. Please send notes with timestamps, one list per song.
Song 2 vocals feel buried in the chorus and the snare is too loud.
Noted. Vocals up 1.5 dB in choruses and snare tucked. v2 tomorrow.
anxieties: How many mix revisions do I have left?
When will the masters be ready for distribution / my release date?
Do I get stems and who owns the masters?
notes: Per-song tracking (each song has its own mix version and revision count). Portal needs audio playback with timestamp comments, version history per song, release-date targets, split sheets and file delivery gated on payment.

label: Podcast production
summary: Weekly video podcast for a consulting firm: editing, show notes, clips and publishing for 4 episodes.
billing: Monthly package for weekly shows ($1,500-3,000 mid-market full service) or per episode for irregular shows ($75-300 editing alone). Sources: Talks.co 2026 pricing guide, Resonate Recordings, The Podcast Consultant.
ms: Done means all 4 episodes for the month are recorded and raw files are received.
Done means each episode's edit is approved by the host.
Done means show notes, transcripts, episode art and 3 clips per episode are approved.
Done means episodes are scheduled on all platforms and the monthly stats are reported.
waiting: Raw recordings uploaded and the host's approval of each edit.
ask: Should guests get to review their episode before release?
checkin: - Done: episodes 41 and 42 published
- Next: edit episode 43
- Needs from you: approve the episode 43 cut and send guest headshot
talk: Episode 43 edit is ready. We cut the 4-minute tangent about the conference; listen at 18:20.
Good cut, but please keep the client story at 22:10.
Restored. Show notes and clips will be in your approval queue by Thursday.
anxieties: Is this week's episode going out on time?
Did you cut anything sensitive / that a guest asked to remove?
How are downloads trending?
notes: Per-episode pipeline inside a monthly retainer; the portal should show each episode's stage. Audio/video review with timestamped comments, guest release forms, and publishing calendar.

label: Copywriting and content
project: Website copy for Turner Landscape Design
summary: Messaging and copy for a 6-page website plus a welcome email sequence.
billing: 50% deposit before work, balance on delivery of approved copy; 2 revision rounds typical, new direction billed as new work; kill fee 25-50% of remaining value. Sources: FemFounded copywriter contract, Susan Greene, Writer's Digest.
ms: Done means the client approved the messaging brief (audience, voice, key messages).
Done means first drafts of all 6 pages are delivered.
Done means two revision rounds are complete and all pages approved.
Done means the welcome sequence is approved and final copy docs are delivered.
waiting: Comments on the first drafts (and the completed intake questionnaire before work starts).
ask: Credibility-led: '20 years of Bay Area landscapes'
Direct: 'Landscape design and build in the East Bay'
Sub copy adapts to the one you pick.
checkin: - Done: drafts for all 6 pages delivered in Google Docs
- Next: round 1 revisions
- Needs from you: comments in the doc by Monday, choose a headline
talk: All 6 page drafts are in the shared folder. Please comment directly in the docs.
Love the services page. Can the about page be more personal?
Yes. Send me a few stories about how you started and I'll weave them in for round 1.
anxieties: How many rounds of edits do I get?
When will copy be ready for the web designer?
Will it sound like us?
notes: Deliverables are documents; review happens in comments. Portal should link docs, track revision rounds, and coordinate handoff to another vendor (web designer). Often part of a bigger project, so fairly standardized.

label: Print and signage shop
project: New storefront signage for Nguyen Bakery
summary: Illuminated channel letter sign, window vinyl and an A-frame for a bakery opening.
billing: Deposit (often 50%) or full payment at estimate approval, balance on install; proof approval and sometimes permit approval required before production. Production about 5-7 business days after proof for print, longer for fabricated signs. Sources: FASTSIGNS ordering process, 4over4, UTMB print shop.
ms: Done means the site is measured and the client approved the estimate and paid the deposit.
Done means the client signed the final proof (colors, size, mounting).
Done means the city permit and landlord approval are in and the sign is fabricated.
Done means the sign is installed, lit and inspected, and the balance is paid.
waiting: Signed proof approval (and the landlord's sign approval for the permit).
ask: Which lighting option for the channel letters?
Halo-lit adds $1,200 and about a week.
answered: Pantone 7621 red faces with white returns.
checkin: - Done: proof v2 sent
- Next: submit permit once proof is signed
- Needs from you: sign the proof and send the landlord approval letter
talk: Proof v2 is ready with the larger logo. Production starts as soon as you sign it.
Looks good, but can the phone number be bigger on the window?
Done in v3, attached. Please sign by Wednesday to keep the install before your opening.
anxieties: Will it be ready before the opening date?
Is the color/size right (what I approved)?
Is the permit approved yet?
notes: Simple, fast jobs (business cards) to permit-gated fabrication. Proof approval is a legally meaningful sign-off and should be recorded with version and timestamp. Portal needs proof versions, a hard 'approve for production' button, permit status, and install scheduling. Many jobs are repeat orders.

label: Animation and motion graphics
project: 90-second animated explainer for a fintech app
summary: 2D animated explainer with voiceover for a budgeting app's homepage and ads.
billing: 50% deposit, 50% on delivery (or thirds: start, after styleframes/storyboard, delivery); revision rounds defined per stage, changes after animation are costly. Sources: video editing contract templates, Filmlifestyle contract guide.
ms: Done means the script is approved and the voiceover recording is approved.
Done means the storyboard and 3 styleframes are approved.
Done means the full animation is reviewed and one round of animation notes applied.
Done means final files in all formats with captions are delivered.
waiting: Storyboard approval, because changes after animation starts cost much more.
ask: Samples are in the review link.
answered: Flat 2D with brand colors, no characters' faces.
checkin: - Done: script and VO approved
- Next: storyboard and styleframes
- Needs from you: brand assets (fonts, icons)
talk: Storyboard is ready. Changes are cheap now and expensive later, so please review closely.
Scene 4 should show the savings screen, not the dashboard.
Swapping it. Updated board tomorrow.
anxieties: When can I see something moving?
What changes are still free at this stage?
Can we update it later when the app UI changes?
notes: Stage-gated approvals where late changes are expensive; the portal should state what is locked at each stage. Video review with frame comments, voiceover file approvals, music licensing.
